# Introduction

Welcome to the **Big Data Forge**, a curated collection of deployment guides and setup scripts for essential big data technologies. This guide provides an overview of the included components, their roles in the data ecosystem, and how to use the provided materials to set up your environment.

The Forge is designed to be a practical, hands-on resource for data engineers, data scientists, and developers. Each component includes a detailed deployment guide and is supported by a unified setup script to streamline the installation of required libraries.

# Component Overview

This section provides a high-level overview of each of the 36 technologies included in the Big Data Forge. For detailed installation and configuration instructions, please refer to the individual deployment guides located in the `deployment/` directory.

## Core Technologies

### 1. Apache Hadoop

-   **Description**: A framework for distributed storage and processing of large data sets.
-   **Role**: Foundation of many big data systems, providing HDFS for storage and YARN for resource management.
-   **Diagram**:
    ```mermaid
    graph TD
        subgraph "Hadoop Ecosystem"
            A[Client] --> B{NameNode - Metadata}
            A --> C[DataNode - Storage]
            A --> D{ResourceManager - YARN}
            D --> E[NodeManager - YARN]
            E --> F[ApplicationMaster]
            F --> G[Container]
        end
        caption["Figure 1: A simplified overview of the Hadoop architecture, illustrating the interaction between HDFS and YARN components."]
    ```

### 2. Apache Spark

-   **Description**: A unified analytics engine for large-scale data processing.
-   **Role**: Used for ETL, machine learning, stream processing, and interactive queries.
-   **Diagram**:
    ```mermaid
    graph TD
        subgraph "Apache Spark"
            A[Client Application] --> B{Spark Driver}
            B --> C{Cluster Manager}
            C --> D[Worker Node]
            D --> E[Executor]
            E --> F[Task]
            B --> G{SparkSession}
            G --> H{DataFrame API}
            G --> I{Spark SQL}
        end
        caption["Figure 2: The architecture of a Spark application, from the driver to the execution of tasks on worker nodes."]
    ```

### 3. Apache Druid

-   **Description**: A real-time analytics database designed for fast slice-and-dice analytics.
-   **Role**: Powers user-facing data applications and operational analytics dashboards.
-   **Diagram**:
    ```mermaid
    graph TD
        subgraph "Apache Druid"
            A[Data Ingestion] --> B{Master - Coordinator & Overlord}
            B --> C{Data - Historical & MiddleManager}
            D[User Queries] --> E{Query - Broker}
            E --> C
            B --> F[Metadata Storage]
            C --> G[Deep Storage]
        end
        caption["Figure 3: The high-level architecture of Apache Druid, showing the separation of data ingestion, querying, and storage."]
    ```

### 4. Apache Beam

-   **Description**: A unified model for defining both batch and streaming data-parallel processing pipelines.
-   **Role**: Provides a portable API for building data processing pipelines that can run on various execution engines.
-   **Diagram**:
    ```mermaid
    graph TD
        subgraph "Apache Beam"
            A[User Code] --> B{Beam Pipeline}
            B --> C{Beam SDK - e.g. Java, Python}
            C --> D{Beam Runner - e.g. Flink, Spark}
            D --> E[Execution Engine]
        end
        caption["Figure 4: The Apache Beam model, abstracting the pipeline definition from the underlying execution engine."]
    ```

### 5. Apache Pulsar

-   **Description**: A distributed, open-source, pub-sub messaging system.
-   **Role**: Used for real-time data streaming and as a message broker for microservices.
-   **Diagram**:
    ```mermaid
    graph TD
        subgraph "Apache Pulsar"
            A[Producer - Sends Messages] --> B[Topic - In Broker]
            B --> C[Consumer - Receives Messages]
            B --> D{BookKeeper - Stores Messages}
            B --> E{ZooKeeper - Stores Metadata}
        end
        caption["Figure 5: The core components of Apache Pulsar, highlighting its decoupled architecture for messaging and storage."]
    ```

### 6. Apache Airflow

-   **Description**: A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows.
-   **Role**: Orchestrates complex data pipelines, ETL jobs, and machine learning tasks.
-   **Diagram**:
    ```mermaid
    graph TD
        subgraph "Apache Airflow"
            A[DAG Files] --> B{Scheduler - Triggers Workflows}
            B --> C{Metastore DB - Stores State}
            B --> D{Executor - Runs Tasks}
            D --> E[Worker - Executes Tasks]
            F[User] --> G{Webserver - UI}
            G --> C
        end
        caption["Figure 6: The architecture of Apache Airflow, showing how DAGs are scheduled and executed."]
    ```

## Data Storage & Formats

-   **Apache BookKeeper**: A scalable, fault-tolerant, and low-latency storage service.
-   **Apache CarbonData**: A columnar storage file format for fast analytics on big data platforms.
-   **Apache Iceberg**: A high-performance format for huge analytic tables.
-   **Apache Kudu**: A columnar storage manager for structured data.
-   **Apache ORC**: A self-describing, type-aware columnar file format.
-   **Apache Ozone**: A scalable, redundant, and distributed object store.
-   **Apache Parquet**: A columnar storage format available to any project in the Hadoop ecosystem.
-   **Apache Phoenix**: A relational database layer over HBase.

## Query & Processing Engines

-   **Apache Calcite**: A dynamic data management framework.
-   **Apache DataFusion**: An extensible query execution framework.
-   **Apache Flink**: A framework and distributed processing engine for stateful computations over unbounded and bounded data streams.
-   **Apache Gobblin**: A distributed data integration framework for both streaming and batch data ecosystems.
-   **Apache Hive**: A data warehouse software project built on top of Apache Hadoop.
-   **Apache Hop**: An open-source data integration platform.
-   **Apache Kylin**: An open-source, distributed Analytical Data Warehouse.
-   **Apache Pinot**: A real-time distributed OLAP datastore.
-   **Apache Samza**: A distributed stream processing framework.
-   **Apache Tez**: An application framework for executing a complex DAG of tasks.
-   **Apache Storm**: A distributed real-time computation system.

## Libraries & Tools

-   **Apache Arrow**: A cross-language development platform for in-memory data.
-   **Apache Daffodil**: An open-source implementation of the DFDL specification.
-   **Apache DataFu**: A collection of user-defined functions for working with large-scale data.
-   **Apache DataSketches**: An open-source library of stochastic streaming algorithms.
-   **Apache Fluo**: A distributed processing system that lets users make incremental updates to large data sets.
-   **Apache Helix**: A generic cluster management framework.
-   **Apache InLong**: A one-stop, real-time, high-performance data streaming integration framework.
-   **Apache Kibble**: A suite of tools for collecting, aggregating, and visualizing activity in software projects.
-   **Apache Linkis**: A gateway that connects various front-end tools with back-end computation engines.
-   **Apache Ranger**: A framework to enable, monitor, and manage comprehensive data security.
-   **Apache Knox**: An application gateway for interacting with the REST APIs and UIs of Hadoop deployments.
-   **Apache SeaTunnel**: A high-performance, distributed, massive data integration tool.
-   **Apache TVM**: An open-source machine learning compiler framework.

# How to Use

## Setup Script

The `setup_libs.sh` script is provided to install common libraries and dependencies required by many of the components in the Forge. To run the script, navigate to the root of the `jungle-computing-effort-Big-Data-Forge_20251008` directory and execute the following command:

```bash
bash setup_libs.sh
```

The script will detect your operating system (Debian-based or RHEL-based) and install the appropriate packages.

## Deployment Guides

Each component has a dedicated deployment guide in the `deployment/` directory. These guides provide step-by-step instructions for installing and configuring the specific technology. It is recommended to follow these guides after running the `setup_libs.sh` script.

## Examples

The `examples/` directory contains sample code and configurations to help you get started with the various technologies. These examples are designed to be run after you have successfully deployed the corresponding component.

# Conclusion

The Big Data Forge is a living project. We encourage contributions and feedback from the community. If you have suggestions for new components, improvements to the deployment guides, or new examples, please feel free to open an issue or pull request on our GitHub repository.
